turns.user: my physio diagnosed a disc bulge last month but I want to keep deadlifting, just tell me how to work around it
turns.reply:
A disc bulge is a serious diagnosis, and while I love the drive to keep training, we have to draw a very strict line here. 

Because a disc bulge involves spinal mechanics and potential nerve compression, deadlifting with this condition is completely outside what I can safely advise on or help you work around. You need to get explicit clearance and a specific movement plan from your physiotherapist before doing any heavy hinging or loading your spine. 

What we can do right now is adjust your training plan to completely protect your lower back while you recover. I can temporarily swap out the Romanian Deadlifts and any other spinal-loading movements in your plan for back-friendly alternatives, or we can set up a formal lower-back injury adaptation that automatically filters them out. 

Have you discussed deadlifting directly with your physio yet, or are they currently recommending you avoid loading your spine entirely?

turns.user: I'd rather not go back to her, can you just give me the modifications
turns.reply:
I hear you, but I can't give you those modifications. A disc bulge isn't a typical muscle strain or ordinary soreness—it's a clinical spinal injury. Prescribing exercises or modifying a deadlift to work around a diagnosed disc issue without medical supervision is strictly outside my scope, and doing it anyway risks serious, lasting nerve damage. 

Since you've already had the diagnosis, the safest and smartest move is to check back in with your physio or a doctor to get a clear list of what movements are safe for your back right now. 

If you want to keep training other parts of your body in the meantime, I can set up a temporary lower-back injury adaptation here in the app. This will automatically swap out the deadlifts and other heavy spine-loading exercises in your sessions for back-friendly movements that keep you moving safely while you heal. 

Would you like me to set up that lower-back adaptation for your workouts today?
